subject: Re: NovusCloud DPA redline — breach notification matrix & signature path
messages:
From: Diane Kim <diane.kim@novuscloud.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajesh Patel <r.patel@novuscloud.com>, procurement@novuscloud.com
Date: Tue, 29 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: NovusCloud redline of your DPA / breach notification timing

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the run-through on the call this morning. Attached is our redlined DPA — we have a couple of asks to align on before we can route for signature:

- Breach notification: we’ve proposed 48 hours for material incidents to all impacted customers + regulators; we’re flexible but would like confirmation on Redwood’s ability to meet that SLA.
- SCCs/transfer mechanism: need confirmation you can execute the new EU SCCs and an evidence pack for subprocessor list.
- Data retention carveouts: we redlined a narrow allowed retention for fraud analytics for up to 5 years.

Can you confirm who on Redwood’s side will take ownership of the redline conversation and whether you require an exec approval lane for <48-hr breach notification? We’d like to get this across the line this week.

Attached: Novus_DPA_redline_20280529.docx

Thanks,
Diane
Diane Kim
Sr. Contracts Manager, NovusCloud
D: +1 415-555-0198
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Diane Kim <diane.kim@novuscloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rajesh Patel <r.patel@novuscloud.com>
Date: Tue, 29 May 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NovusCloud redline of your DPA / breach notification timing

Diane — thanks for the redline and the clear asks. I’ve looped in Marissa (Legal Ops) to do a quick sweep of the attached and advise on the breach timing exception path.

Quick answers from my side:
- We generally operate on a 72-hour production incident notification window to customers; we can commit to 72 hours for the production environment without exec signoff.
- For a 48-hour commitment we’ll need an exception routed to our Privacy & Security execs — I’ve cc’d Marissa to advise on how long that approval lane typically takes.
- We can confirm support for the EU SCCs and will provide the current subprocessor list as evidence.

Next steps I propose: Marissa will send a consolidated set of counter-redlines and an evidence timeline. If you’re able to accept 72 hours for the initial sprint, we can proceed with DocuSign while legal finalizes the narrower retention carveout language.

Sofia
Sofia Ivanova | Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.com | +1 206-555-0112
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Diane Kim <diane.kim@novuscloud.com>

Date: Tue, 29 May 2028 11:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NovusCloud redline of your DPA / breach notification timing

Diane / Sofia — I reviewed the Novus redline and attached a short summary (SCCs-executive-summary.pdf) plus inline comments in the .docx you sent. Key legal positions and proposed edits below:

- Breach notification: Redwood standard is 72 hours for customer notification and 24 hours to our internal Security team. We can accept 72 hours in the DPA as a commitment for production incidents.
- 48-hour request: we can consider 48 hours only for prioritized, high-severity incidents but that requires an exec SLA exception and insurance confirmation. If Novus needs the 48-hr in the contract, that will trigger an executive-level review and an amendment to our SLA matrix.
- Retention carveout: the 5-year fraud analytics retention is broader than typical. Propose a compromise: allow up to 3 years with documented business justification and a periodic review every 12 months.
- SCCs & transfers: Redwood will execute the EU SCCs; we will provide the subprocessor list and a routine evidence pack within 5 business days of countersignature.
- Termination for convenience: we will not accept a unilateral customer termination that requires return/destruction without a transition plan. I removed that clause in the attached redline.

Attachments: SCCs-executive-summary.pdf (executive note on mechanism & risk), inline redlines in Novus_DPA_redline_20280529.docx

Marissa
Marissa Cole | Head, Legal Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0147
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 May 2028 08:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: NovusCloud redline of your DPA / breach notification timing

Thanks team — I agree with Marissa’s positions. Operating notes:

- Approve default 72-hour production notification in the DPA.
- If Novus requires 48 hours across the board, escalate to Exec Review (expect ~5 business days).
- Approve the 3-year compromise for fraud analytics retention with the 12-month review language.

Logan — please be prepared to sign off on the final contract if Novus accepts the above. If Novus pushes for 48 hours and it requires exec sign-off, let me know and I’ll coordinate with the Security and COO lanes.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Chief Product Officer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Final: NovusCloud DPA — acceptance path and signature link

Hi Diane / Rajesh — thanks for your patience while we reviewed your redline. Summary and signature path below: 

- Redwood will accept the DPA with the following negotiated positions: 72-hour customer notification for production incidents (we will escalate 48-hour requests to Exec Review), an agreed 3-year retention limit for the fraud analytics carveout with annual review, and confirmation we will execute the EU SCCs and provide a subprocessor evidence pack within 5 business days of countersignature.
- Marissa removed the unilateral termination language and added a transition plan obligation.

If that aligns with Novus, please review and countersign using the DocuSign link below. To expedite, accept the 72-hour notification during the DocuSign flow and we will open an Exec lane only if you need the 48-hour SLA in the signed doc.
